e: Unadapted borrowing from Norwegian krumkake (“curved cake”). Compare Middle English crumcake, cramkake (“loaf of unleavened bread; a twisted or crumpled cake”).
From German Krummhorn, from krumm (“crooked”) + Horn (“horn”). Doublet of cromorna.
From Ancient Greek κρυπτάδια (kruptádia), neuter plural form of κρυπτάδιος (kruptádios, “secret”).

e: Borrowed from Indonesian krupuk or kerupuk, derived from Javanese ꦏꦿꦸꦥꦸꦏ꧀ (krupuk), inherited from Old Javanese kerupuk. Cognate with Dutch kroepoek.
Named after Czech mineralogist Tomáš Krut'a (1906–1998), + -ite.
Early 21st century, probably an alteration of crunk.
